resolution.note: The launcher waits past Herdr's unknown to the successor's first classified status and prints it; a blocked successor exits 0 with a stderr line naming its pane and tab, and the handoff stands. Verbatim Herdr 0.9.1 captures agent-get-unknown-claude and agent-get-blocked-claude (folder-trust dialog). Live probe from a scratch shell pane: successor: herdr tab w1D:tAX pane w1D:pB2 agent claude blocked, exit 0 in 6 s. krn-handoff relays that line and never relaunches.

title: Report a successor that waits on a startup dialog
body:
Outcome: the launcher's success line shows the successor's first settled Herdr status, and a successor waiting on a startup dialog (`blocked`) is reported to the operator with its pane instead of passing as a clean handoff.
Evidence: the t-p4akh87 live probe (Herdr 0.9.1, untrusted scratch cwd) printed `successor: herdr tab w1D:tAR pane w1D:pAX agent claude unknown` within 3 s while the pane sat on Claude's folder-trust dialog; `herdr agent get` reported `blocked` seconds later. A project MCP approval or a login prompt would stall a real handoff the same way. The official `agent start` fails with agent_not_ready on such a dialog while the agent is live, so failing the launch risks a duplicate successor (t-tdkpgag): report, do not fail.
Proof: a test with a verbatim blocked `agent get` capture (redacted per test/fixtures/README.md) where the new pane goes from unknown to blocked prints `agent claude blocked` and exits 0; the krn-handoff skill tells the predecessor to name that pane in its report.

Live probe: run the launcher from a scratch Herdr tab whose pane hosts only a shell (herdr tab create --cwd <scratch> --no-focus; herdr pane run <pane> 'KRN_SUCCESSOR_AGENT=claude node <repo>/scripts/claude/successor-launch.ts ...'), never from the lead's pane: a lead caller gets its tab renamed and the probe successor's --retire closes the lead pane once idle. A shell caller has no agent, so the launcher skips the rename, the ledger and the predecessor env; close both tabs afterwards. An untrusted scratch cwd holds the probe on the folder-trust dialog, so it spends no tokens.
